title: Six of a Family Killed in Fire at Home Above Grocery Store in Maharashtra
excerpt: In Yedshi village, Dharashiv district, Govind and Jyoti Karande carried their son downstairs to safety, then went back into the burning home for their daughters and parents. All six who remained upstairs died.
body:
• Six members of the Karande family — grandparents aged 75 and 70, a couple aged 47 and 42, and their daughters aged 16 and 15 — died in a fire at their home above the family grocery store in Yedshi village, Dharashiv district, in the early hours of Monday, November 9.
  • The couple's young son, Krishna, was the sole survivor: his parents brought him downstairs to safety, then went back up to try to rescue the others and were trapped as the fire intensified.
  • Police say the cause is still under investigation. Residents told police the family had been awake until about 2 a.m. celebrating Lakshmi Puja; police have not established whether firecrackers played any role.
  • Police said cooking oil, ghee containers and stacks of disposable leaf plates stored in the home appear to have fed the rapid spread of the flames.

Six members of a family were killed in a fire at their home above their grocery store in Yedshi village, in Maharashtra's Dharashiv district, in the early hours of Monday, November 9, The Hindu reported. The fire broke out at about 2:30 a.m. at the residence of Govind Uttam Karande, 47, whose family lived on the upper floor of the building that housed their grocery store.

The dead are Uttam Trimbak Karande, 75, and his wife Chandrakala, 70; their son Govind, 47, and his wife Jyoti, 42; and the couple's daughters Gayatri, 16, and Siddhi, 15. According to Senior Police Inspector Vasudev More of Dharashiv Rural police station, Govind and Jyoti suffered severe burns, while the other four died after inhaling smoke and fumes. Post-mortem reports were awaited, and the bodies were taken to Civil Hospital, Dharashiv, for examination.

A son carried to safety, parents who went back

The couple's son Krishna, whose age was not given, was the family's sole survivor. Inspector More said Govind and Jyoti first brought Krishna downstairs to safety, then returned to the upper floor to try to rescue the elderly couple and their two daughters, asking Krishna to fetch water in buckets. The fire intensified rapidly and trapped all six upstairs.

A driver working for a travel company noticed the fire on the upper floor and alerted the family, Inspector More said. Local residents rushed to the scene and tried to put out the blaze, and fire brigade personnel were deployed, but the intensity of the fire made it difficult to bring under control.

Cause not yet established

Police said the origin and cause of the fire remain under investigation. Local residents told police the family had been awake until about 2 a.m. celebrating Lakshmi Puja and bursting firecrackers, but Inspector More said police had not established whether the firecrackers were connected to the blaze. In the police's preliminary assessment, cooking oil, containers of ghee and stacks of disposable leaf plates kept in the home contributed to how fast the flames spread — a reminder of how much combustible stock a home above a shop can hold.

Inspector More said police had yet to record the statements of Krishna and his uncle, and that an accidental death report would be registered after those statements are recorded. Prakash Vhatkar, an official from the Dharashiv Revenue Office, was among the officials cited in the reporting. No official has announced a cause, compensation or a completed inquiry, and none should be assumed until police finish their investigation.

The deaths came on a Diwali night that produced other fatal fires elsewhere in central India, but police in Dharashiv are treating the Yedshi fire as its own case, with its own unanswered question: how a fire noticed in time for one child to be carried out still left no way back for the six people who remained inside.
